card: Adds a request completion deadline to the HTTP server to disconnect clients that fail to finish sending a request within the -rpcservertimeout window. Currently, the timeout only measures read inactivity and resets on every incoming byte, allowing a slowloris-style trickle of data to hold a connection slot indefinitely without passing authentication. With connection slots capped at 16 by default, this can lock out all legitimate RPC traffic. The author characterizes this as a robustness fix rather than a remote vulnerability because the RPC interface binds to localhost by default.
changed_since_previous: Rebased following related HTTP changes; the core deadline logic and test coverage remain the same as the previous version.
evidence: Author reproduction: 'start a node with -rpcmaxconnections=2, open two sockets, and write "GET / HTTP/1.1\r\n" one byte at a time with ten seconds between bytes. bitcoin-cli getblockcount then hangs until one of the (trickling) sockets is closed.'

Author states: 'Because no request ever completes the authentication functions are never hit. The impact is low because RPC port binds to localhost by default, so this is a robustness fix rather than a remotely exploitable security issue.'
problem: The existing -rpcservertimeout only tracks inactivity between socket reads. A client trickling bytes slowly without finishing a request resets the idle timer continuously, holding a connection slot indefinitely without triggering authentication checks. With default limits (16 slots or -rpcmaxconnections), an attacker or malfunctioning local client can exhaust all slots and block legitimate RPC callers.

risk.why: Flaws in the HTTP deadline or disconnect logic could prematurely abort legitimate requests or disrupt the HTTP server loop, causing RPC denial of service.

summary: Adds a completion deadline to the internal HTTP server to disconnect clients that take too long to send a complete request. The deadline is initialized when the first byte of a request arrives, expires after -rpcservertimeout seconds, and is not extended by subsequent incoming bytes. It is cleared once request parsing completes, deferred while worker threads process a request, restarted while response bytes are being sent, and disabled when -rpcservertimeout=0.
